This guide takes a new analysis from input preparation to a reproducible result directory. It uses the command-line interface because the same workflow works in Docker, Podman, Apptainer, and a local R installation.

## 1. Choose the analysis mode

popgenVCF determines which analyses are scientifically available from the supplied inputs.

| Mode | Required input | Analyses that can become available |
|---|---|---|
| VCF only | Diploid biallelic SNP VCF | QC, filtering, LD pruning, PCA, IBS/MDS, kinship (KING-robust), genetic sex check, runs of homozygosity, and configured ancestry engines |
| Sample metadata | VCF plus exact sample identifiers | VCF-only analyses with descriptive annotations |
| Population metadata | Complete `population` values | Diversity, FST, genome scans, DAPC, AMOVA, and population summaries |
| Spatial metadata | Usable `latitude` and `longitude` values | Mantel, isolation-by-distance, maps, and spatial analyses |

Missing metadata does not make a VCF-only analysis invalid. Modules whose requirements are not met are skipped transparently and recorded in `analysis_capabilities.tsv`.

## 2. Prepare the VCF and metadata

The VCF sample names are immutable sample keys. When metadata are supplied,
the `sample` column must match every VCF sample name exactly, once and only
once. An optional `alias` supplies a clearer public label without renaming the
VCF/GDS identity.

```text
sample	alias	population	latitude	longitude	location
Sample01	Ottawa_01	North	45.4215	-75.6972	Ottawa
Sample02	NA	North	45.4200	-75.6900	Ottawa
Sample03	Montreal_01	South	45.5019	-73.5674	Montreal
Sample04	Montreal_02	South	NA	NA	Montreal
```

Use signed decimal degrees: latitude is positive north/negative south and
longitude is positive east/negative west. Use `NA` for missing optional
values. A missing alias falls back to `sample`; incomplete coordinates exclude
only that sample from spatial calculations. In contrast, any missing
`population` value disables population-dependent modules. Never omit a sample
row: the metadata and VCF sample sets must match exactly.

See the [complete metadata guide](metadata.html) for accepted columns,
identity fields, coordinate ranges, missing-data rules, and validation checks.

The input VCF may be uncompressed, ordinary gzip-compressed, or BGZF-compressed. popgenVCF reuses a valid index and otherwise creates a sorted BGZF copy and Tabix index in the analysis cache. Preserve the original input and record its checksum before analysis.

## 3. Select an executable environment

For exploratory work, define an image variable once:

```bash
export POPGENVCF_IMAGE="ghcr.io/duceppemo/popgenvcf:latest"
```

For a publication or archive, replace `latest` with the immutable digest recorded by the corresponding GitHub Release:

```bash
export POPGENVCF_IMAGE="ghcr.io/duceppemo/popgenvcf@sha256:<digest>"
```

A local package installation can use the same CLI arguments through `Rscript inst/cli/popgenVCF.R`.

## 4. Generate and edit the configuration

From the directory containing the VCF and metadata:

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$PWD:/data" \
  "$POPGENVCF_IMAGE" \
  --write-config /data/analysis.yml
```

`--write-config` detects the logical CPUs and memory available to the current
process, including Docker CPU affinity/quota and memory limits when present.
The generated YAML lists every built-in analysis. Population- and
geography-dependent analyses are initially set to `no`; PCA, IBS, and the
neighbour-joining tree remain available from VCF sample IDs alone. Optional
external ancestry backends are listed but disabled.

Edit at least the input and output sections:

```yaml
input:
  vcf: /data/cohort.vcf.gz
  metadata: /data/metadata.tsv
  metadata_header: auto

output:
  directory: /data/results
  figure_formats: [pdf, png]
  dpi: 600
  figure_style: accessibility-first
  base_font_size: 11
  label_samples: auto

compute:
  threads: 8
  memory_mb: 32768
  seed: 42

qc:
  maf: 0.05
  max_sample_missing: 0.20

report:
  enabled: true
  title: Population genomic analysis
  author: Analyst name
```

Container paths must be visible inside the container. With the bind mount above, host files under the current directory appear under `/data`.

The default `accessibility-first` figure style uses colour-vision-aware palettes and redundant point shapes where the plot geometry permits them. Use `grayscale-safe` for monochrome publication, and add `svg` to `figure_formats` when you need editable vector artwork. See the [publication figure styles guide](https://github.com/duceppemo/popgenVCF/blob/main/docs/PUBLICATION_FIGURE_STYLES.md) for export and palette details.

## 5. Run the analysis

```bash
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  -e HOME=/tmp \
  -v "$PWD:/data" \
  "$POPGENVCF_IMAGE" \
  --config /data/analysis.yml
```

On an HPC system, use the equivalent Apptainer command from the [containers and HPC guide](containers-and-hpc.html). Generate the template inside the allocation when possible, and set `compute.threads` and `compute.memory_mb` no higher than the scheduler allocation.

## 6. Inspect the execution evidence first

Before interpreting figures, review the machine-readable control files in the result root:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `pipeline.log` | Ordered operational log and failures |
| `analysis_capabilities.tsv` | Available and skipped modules with reasons |
| `analysis_execution_plan.tsv` | Dependency-resolved execution plan |
| `analysis_execution_ledger.tsv` | Success, failure, blocking, retry, or timeout state |
| `analysis_module_contracts.tsv` | Registered module requirements and contracts |
| `analysis_artifacts.tsv` | Produced artifact manifest when artifacts exist |
| `analysis_validation.tsv` | Module validation outcomes when validation records exist |
| `analysis_summary.tsv` | Stable analysis summary |
| `report/population_genomics_report.html` | Portable human-readable report with tables and embedded figures |
| `report/population_genomics_report.pdf` | Compact, email-friendly report using vector figures when available |
| `analysis_results.rds` | Complete serialized analysis object for R-based reproducibility and report regeneration |
| `sessionInfo.txt` | R and package environment |

The `tables/` directory begins with sample identity and QC evidence, including `01_sample_QC.tsv`, `02_sample_metadata_match.tsv`, variant-QC tables, and the exact LD-pruned SNP list. Module-specific tables and figures depend on capability and configuration.

Open `report/population_genomics_report.html` in a standard web browser or use
`report/population_genomics_report.pdf` for email, printing, and document
review. Both reports are self-contained and can be copied without the RDS file
or the `figures/` directory. The PDF prefers the existing vector figure files,
which usually makes it substantially smaller than the HTML report. The RDS file
is not intended to be opened by a general-purpose document viewer.

After updating popgenVCF, an existing completed analysis can be converted to the
new report format without rerunning the scientific analyses:

```r
popgenVCF::render_report(
  "results/analysis_results.rds",
  "results/report",
  title = "Population genomics analysis"
)
```

Both formats are requested by default. Pass `formats = "pdf"` to generate only
the compact PDF, or `formats = "html"` to generate only the browser report. PDF
generation requires XeLaTeX, LuaLaTeX, or pdfLaTeX in the execution environment.
When no supported LaTeX engine is available, popgenVCF records a warning, skips
the PDF, and still produces the HTML report.

For many high-resolution plots, the self-contained HTML can be tens of
megabytes and may take a few minutes to generate. This is expected because the
images are embedded in the report for portability.

## 7. Inspect the result from R

```r
analysis <- readRDS("results/analysis_results.rds")
summary(analysis)
popgenVCF::list_analyses()
popgenVCF::get_analysis_result(analysis, "pca")
```

Do not assume that a missing result is a software error. Confirm whether the module was unavailable, skipped, blocked by a failed dependency, or explicitly not selected.

## 8. Validate before interpretation

A completed command is not by itself scientific validation. Check that:

1. sample identities and metadata alignment are correct;
2. retained sample and variant counts are plausible;
3. module validation records pass;
4. no required module is failed, blocked, or timed out;
5. external-tool results record the executable and version actually used;
6. diagnostic-only comparisons are not presented as release-gating equivalence evidence.

Use the [interpretation guide](interpreting-results.html) for analysis-specific cautions.

## 9. Archive the analysis

Retain together:

- the original VCF and metadata checksums;
- `analysis.yml`;
- the exact package version, source commit, or OCI digest;
- the complete result directory;
- external-tool versions and commands;
- scheduler resources, thread count, and random seed;
- validation, benchmark, and provenance evidence relevant to the analysis.

The 0.10.0 software contracts support canonical validation and release evidence, but users must not describe a production baseline, external concordance suite, or release certificate as approved unless the corresponding approval records are present.
